subject: Science
title: Looking after our world
objectives: Children will put litter in a bin and say why we keep places clean.
Children will turn off a tap after use.
content: Putting litter in the bin, keeping the school clean, and saving water.
teachingActivities: Use clean, safe litter such as paper and clean plastic for practice; never touch real litter; model putting litter in the bin; show a tap being turned off; link to the school compound.
learnerActivities: Put litter in a bin, say why we keep places clean and turn off a tap after use.
resources: Clean paper and empty plastic bottles for pretend litter
A class bin and a recycling box
Pictures of a clean and a littered place
assessment: Observe whether each child puts litter in a bin and turns off a tap with support.
expectedOutcomes: Turns off a tap with support.

lessons.title: Litter in the bin
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will put litter in a bin and say why.
successCriteria: Puts pretend litter in a bin
Says litter goes in the bin
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to care for plants, animals and themselves.
resources: Clean paper and empty plastic bottles
Pictures of a clean and a littered place
lessons.starter: Show a picture of a littered playground and say "This place is dirty. How can we make it clean?"
teacherActivities: Show a picture of a clean place and say "This is nice."
Drop a clean paper on the floor and say "Oh no, litter!" Pick it up and put it in the bin.
Let each child pick up pretend litter and put it in the bin.
learnerActivities: Child puts litter in the bin.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a picture of a clean place and say "This is nice." Children: Children look and say clean.
Step 2. Teacher: Drop a clean paper on the floor and say "Oh no, litter!" Pick it up and put it in the bin. Children: Children watch and say bin.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child pick up pretend litter and put it in the bin. Children: Child puts litter in the bin.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Where does litter go?" Children: Child points to the bin.

practical.title: Litter in the bin
steps: Scatter clean paper on the floor.
Children pick it up and put it in the bin.
practical.safety: Use only clean paper and plastic and never let children touch real litter. Wash hands after. An adult handles anything unsafe.

differentiation.support: Pick up the paper together and put it in the bin.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend why we use bins.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says litter goes in the bin
lessons.conclusion: Look at the clean floor and say "Well done."
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child how to put litter in a bin at home and outside.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put litter in a bin and say why" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Pick it up, pick it up, put it in the bin.

lessons.title: Keeping our school clean
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will help to keep their classroom and playground tidy.
successCriteria: Helps to sweep or wipe with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to care for plants, animals and themselves.
lessons.starter: Look around the room and say "Our classroom is messy. Let us make it tidy."
teacherActivities: Show how to put toys in baskets.
Show how to wipe a table with a cloth.
Show how to sweep with a small broom.
Look at the tidy room together.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to put toys in baskets. Children: Children put toys in baskets.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to wipe a table with a cloth. Children: Child wipes a table.
Step 3. Teacher: Show how to sweep with a small broom. Children: Child sweeps with support.
Step 4. Teacher: Look at the tidy room together. Children: Child says tidy or clean.

practical.title: Tidy up time
steps: Sweep the floor with a small broom.
practical.safety: Use child-size tools and supervise closely. Wipe only with clean water and never use cleaning chemicals with children.

differentiation.support: Tidy together and name each job.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say which job they like best.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do with toys?

expectedOutcomes: Helps to keep the room tidy
lessons.conclusion: Look at the tidy room and say "Thank you, helpers."
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child a small tidying job at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "help to keep their classroom and playground tidy" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Saving water
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will turn off a tap after use and say why we save water.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to care for plants, animals and themselves.
resources: A basin with a tap or a jug with a tap
Pictures of a dripping tap and a tap turned off
lessons.starter: Show a dripping tap picture and say "Drip, drip, drip. The water is wasted."
teacherActivities: Show how to turn off a tap tightly after washing.
Let each child turn on a tap, wash hands and turn it off.
Collect a cup of water from the tap and talk about how precious water is.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to turn off a tap tightly after washing. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child turn on a tap, wash hands and turn it off. Children: Child turns off the tap.
Step 3. Teacher: Collect a cup of water from the tap and talk about how precious water is. Children: Children look at the water.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We save water." Children: Children say the sentence.

practical.title: Turn off the tap
practical.safety: Supervise every child at the tap and keep floors dry. Use only clean water for plants.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend why we save water.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do after washing?

lessons.conclusion: Look at the dry tap and say "No drips."
lessons.homeConnection: Turn off the tap together at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "turn off a tap after use and say why we save water" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our clean-up team
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will work as a team to tidy the playground.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to care for plants, animals and themselves.
lessons.starter: Say "We are the clean-up team. Let us make our playground clean and safe."
teacherActivities: Check the playground first and remove any real litter or sharp things yourself.
Put out clean pretend litter and let children collect it.
Put the pretend litter in the bin.
Look at the clean playground and cheer.
learnerActivities: Child picks up pretend litter and puts it in a bucket.
Child puts litter in the bin.
Children clap and say well done.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Check the playground first and remove any real litter or sharp things yourself. Children: Children wait together.
Step 2. Teacher: Put out clean pretend litter and let children collect it. Children: Child picks up pretend litter and puts it in a bucket.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the pretend litter in the bin. Children: Child puts litter in the bin.
Step 4. Teacher: Look at the clean playground and cheer. Children: Children clap and say well done.

practical.title: Clean-up team
steps: Spread clean pretend litter on the playground.
practical.safety: An adult must clear real litter and sharp objects first. Children touch only the clean pretend litter and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Work beside the child and pick up together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how they helped.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say "We are a team."
lessons.homeConnection: Help your family tidy the compound.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "work as a team to tidy the playground" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 environment check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child cares for the environment.
successCriteria: Turns off a tap with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to care for plants, animals and themselves.
lessons.starter: Sing the pick it up song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: litter, tidying and tap.
At each station ask "What do we do?" and watch.
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: litter, tidying and tap. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What do we do?" and watch. Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Environment stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors dry. Use only clean pretend litter.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell a friend how to care for the world.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: puts litter in a bin; helps to tidy; turns off a tap; says we save water.

questions.question: What do we do with a tap?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
lessons.homeConnection: Keep caring for the world at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child cares for the environment" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
